en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Training Rule on Carrying a Staff:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to one carrying a staff.
… [as before] … “‘I will not teach the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is carrying a staff’—this training is to be observed.
The staff for a man of medium height is four cubits long.
Anything longer than that is "excessive," anything shorter is "insufficient.
The Dhamma should not be taught to one who is not ill and does not carry a staff.
Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is holding a staff, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional … [and so forth] …
The eighth training rule is concluded.
